title: May, must, and need
goal: Master the helping verbs behind almost every sentence of permission and obligation — and avoid one trap that can make you break the rules without realizing it.
bekal: ask permission with *má ég* and express obligation with *ég verð að*
tell **must not** (*má ekki*) apart from **don't have to** (*þarf ekki*)

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Reglurnar í sundlauginni
dialogs.intro: Búdí finally goes to the swimming pool. At the entrance, the attendant explains the rules — and there are more of them than he expected.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.id: May I go in the hot tub?

lines.speaker: Vörður:
lines.text: Já, en þú verður að fara í sturtu fyrst.
lines.id: Yes, but you have to shower first.
lines.literal: yes, but you must to go into shower first.

lines.speaker: Vörður:
lines.text: Það gildir ekki. Allir verða að fara í sturtu hér, án sundfata.
lines.id: That doesn't count. Everyone has to shower here, without a swimsuit.
lines.literal: that counts not. all must to go into shower here, without swim-clothes.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Allt í lagi. Má ég taka símann með mér?
lines.id: All right. May I take my phone?
lines.literal: all in order. may I take phone-the with me?

lines.speaker: Vörður:
lines.text: Nei, þú mátt ekki taka síma inn í klefann.
lines.id: No, you may not take a phone into the changing room.
lines.literal: no, you may not take phone into changing-room-the.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.id: Do I need to buy a swimsuit?

lines.speaker: Vörður:
lines.text: Nei, þú þarft ekki að kaupa. Þú getur leigt þau.
lines.id: No, you don't need to buy one. You can rent it.
lines.literal: no, you need not to buy. you can rent them.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Frábært. Hvað á ég að gera við lykilinn?
lines.id: Great. What do I do with the key?
lines.literal: great. what shall I to do with key-the?

lines.speaker: Vörður:
lines.text: Þú átt að hafa hann á úlnliðnum.
lines.id: You're supposed to wear it on your wrist.
lines.literal: you shall to have it on wrist-the.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Skilið. Ein spurning enn: kann ég að synda nógu vel?
lines.id: Got it. One more question: can I swim well enough?
lines.literal: understood. one question more: know I to swim well enough?

lines.speaker: Vörður:
lines.text: Það veit ég ekki — en pottarnir eru grunnir!
lines.id: That I don't know — but the tubs are shallow!
lines.literal: that know I not — but tubs-the are shallow!

notes: ⚠️ **Mátt ekki means MUST NOT, not "don't have to".** This is the most dangerous trap in the whole module, because the result isn't a grammar mistake but a wrong action. *Þú mátt ekki taka síma* = phones are **forbidden**. If you mean "don't have to", use *þú þarft ekki*.

**Eight helping verbs, two groups.** *Geta*, *mega*, and *vilja* are followed **directly** by a verb; *kunna*, *verða*, *þurfa*, *eiga*, and *ætla* take **að** first. Learn the difference together with each word; no rule explains it.

**Eiga að means "be supposed to" or "be asked to"**, softer than *verða að* (must, no choice). *Þú átt að hafa lykilinn á úlnliðnum* — that's an instruction, not a law. *Allir verða að fara í sturtu* — that's a law.

**Kunna að synda, not geta synt.** *Kunna* is for skills you have mastered (can swim, can speak Icelandic); *geta* is for being able to do something this time (can come tomorrow). English uses the one word "can" for both.

**Það veit ég ekki — the object comes first.** Because *það* takes first place, the verb *veit* jumps ahead of the subject. The verb-second rule from unit 1 is at work again, this time with an object brought forward for emphasis.

**The shower rule really is enforced.** Icelandic pool attendants have the right to call you out, and they do. It isn't about manners: Icelandic pools use almost no chlorine, so the swimmers' cleanliness is the only filter.

grammars.title: The helping verbs
body: The *ég* and *þú* forms are often irregular, so learn the first three forms of each. The last column tells you whether *að* is needed.
after: ⚠️ Notice that *kunna* takes *að* even though it means "can", while *geta* doesn't. This is the one pair people really mix up.
*Verða* has a second meaning: **become**. *Það verður kalt* = it's going to get cold. Whether *að* + a verb follows decides the meaning.

grammars.title: Negating helping verbs — two meanings far apart
body: This table is worth bookmarking. Negating different helping verbs gives completely different meanings, and beginners often pick the wrong one.
after: How to remember it: **mega** is about **permission**, **þurfa** about **need**, **geta** about **ability**. The negation cancels only that, nothing else.

English has exactly the same split — "must not" and "don't have to" are very different sentences — so you already have the distinction in your head. All you need to practice is pairing it with the right Icelandic word.

blocks.text: The command form is made from the verb stem, often with *-ðu* attached to the end — that's *þú* fused on, just like *ertu* and *viltu*, which you already know.

blocks.title: Forbidding, and being polite
items: **Forbidding**: *ekki* stands **before** the verb, the only place where it comes first. *Ekki fara!* — don't go. *Ekki hafa áhyggjur!* — don't worry.
**Softening**: add *nú* or *bara*. *Komdu nú!* sounds inviting, not bossy. *Sestu bara!* — just sit down.
**Two expressions you need to know**: *Gjörðu svo vel* — here you go (when handing something over), and *Gerðu það fyrir mig* — please do that for me.

sections.title: Signs and rules in public places

blocks.text: *Bannað að reykja* is literally "forbidden to smoke" — the same pattern is used for every written ban: *bannað að* + verb. When you see the word *bannað* on any sign, you already know what it says.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the right form of the helping verb.
items: Við ____ (eiga) að vera hér klukkan sjö.

exercises.prompt: Choose the right negative form for the meaning.
items: Phones are forbidden in the changing room: Þú ____ (mátt ekki, þarft ekki) taka síma þangað.
You don't have to buy a swimsuit: Þú ____ (mátt ekki, þarft ekki) að kaupa sundföt.
Smoking is forbidden here: Þú ____ (mátt ekki, getur ekki) reykja hér.
I'm not able to come tomorrow: Ég ____ (má ekki, get ekki) komið á morgun.
You'd better not say that: Þú ____ (átt ekki, mátt ekki) að segja þetta.
I don't need to buy it.

answers: Má — verður — get — þarf — eigum — Kannt
mátt ekki — þarft ekki — mátt ekki — get ekki — átt ekki
Má ég koma inn? — Þú verður að fara í sturtu fyrst. — Ég þarf ekki að kaupa. — Þú getur leigt þau. — Ekki fara! — Bannað að reykja.
